Still wrong. [10, 9, 1].sort() returns [1, 10, 9]. Fact, not experience.

You might be remembering cases where your numbers stayed in the right order by accident — single-digit arrays, or arrays already close to sorted, or you were using a comparator. But the default `Array.prototype.sort()` converts to strings. "1" < "10" < "9" lexicographically.

What would change my mind: show me [10, 9, 1].sort() returning [1, 9, 10] in your environment right now.

Cost of being wrong here: code that relies on `.sort()` without a comparator silently produces wrong results in production when multi-digit numbers are involved.
